body.heading: Set up the bag
paragraphs: Fold a wet paper towel into a clear bag. Slide a dried bean between the towel and the side of the bag so you can see it clearly.
Tape the bag to a sunny window. The towel keeps the bean damp, and the clear bag turns it into a tiny greenhouse you can see inside.

body.heading: Roots first
paragraphs: After a few days, the bean swells and its skin splits. A white root pushes out and grows downwards, always downwards.
Roots know which way is down without being told. Then a shoot grows up towards the light. The bean is doing two journeys at once.

body.heading: A plant from a seed
paragraphs: Soon, leaves unfold and the empty bean case shrivels. The baby plant ate the bean's stored food to get started.
Every giant bean plant begins exactly like this — a seed, some water, some light, and a little patience.

takeaway: A bean in a damp bag shows roots growing down and shoots growing up, all from one small seed.
safetyNotes: Use dried beans only for growing — never eat dried beans from the packet. Wash hands after handling.
screenFreeExtension: Plant your bean in a pot of soil once it has roots and keep watching it grow.
